name: Citizenship by Registration (Marriage)

requirement_groups.name: Foreign woman married to a Ghanaian man

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign woman who marries a Ghanaian man may acquire Ghanaian nationality on marriage, without an additional residency requirement.

requirement_groups.name: Foreign man married to a Ghanaian woman

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign man married to a Ghanaian woman must first establish permanent residency in Ghana before he can acquire citizenship through the marriage -- registration remains discretionary, and marriage alone does not guarantee citizenship.
requirements.fix_path: Establish permanent residency in Ghana while the marriage subsists.

evidence_required.document: Proof of permanent residency in Ghana (foreign-husband track)

sources.title: Wikipedia -- Ghanaian nationality law: 'a foreign women who married a Ghanaian man could immediately acquire nationality', while a foreign man married to a Ghanaian woman must establish permanent residency in Ghana before acquiring citizenship through marriage

Ghana Citizenship (private legal-service site) -- Ghana Citizenship Act 2000 (Act 591), Section 10: marriage route described as discretionary approval for spouses of Ghanaian citizens, with marriage alone not guaranteeing citizenship -- read alongside the Wikipedia source, this appears to describe the foreign-husband track specifically rather than a uniformly gender-neutral rule

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ghana). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-3/tier-4 sourcing only; Ghana's own Act 591 text was not directly fetchable in this build. MARQUEE GENDERED FINDING, CONSISTENT WITH A PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY IN THIS DATASET (Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria, Sudan, Somalia, Pakistan): a foreign woman marrying a Ghanaian man acquires citizenship immediately on marriage with no residency requirement, while a foreign man marrying a Ghanaian woman must first establish permanent residency in Ghana -- and even then, per the ghanacitizenship.com source, registration remains a discretionary Presidential-approval process rather than an entitlement. This is one of the more starkly asymmetric marriage provisions found in this dataset: one path is close to automatic, the other requires establishing an entirely separate legal status (permanent residency) first, with no guarantee of citizenship even then. Two independent tier-3/4 sources agree on the direction of the asymmetry, though neither could be corroborated against the Act's primary text directly in this build.
